schedule_id.meaning: Schedule id; HTTP reads schedule_id and the CLI uses its positional id.

round.meaning: CLI --round selects round rather than owner trigger; a disabled schedule is refused for round.

wait.meaning: CLI --wait waits for the queued fire to reach a terminal state.

deadline_seconds.meaning: CLI --deadline-seconds requires --wait and a positive integer. Without an explicit deadline, --wait uses max_seconds + 300 seconds.

ok.meaning: Whether queuing or the requested wait succeeded.

fire_id.meaning: Identifier of the queued fire, on the non-waiting success path. The public queue wrapper removes its internal max_seconds before both CLI and HTTP replies.

state.meaning: Queued on a successful non-waiting queue.

fire.meaning: On CLI --wait, the observed fire row, or null when not available.

signal.meaning: CLI argument or wait failure, or a queue refusal when --round is selected. Open forms include <raw SQLite, filesystem or socket error text>, <stored JSON parser error text>, pid2-schedule-needs-unmet: <routine>/<line>, pid2-schedule-wait-socket: <error>, and pid2-command-wake-persist-failed: <error>.

firstMissingSignal.meaning: The enum lists fixed literal outcomes. Open forms can also appear: <raw SQLite or filesystem error text>, <stored JSON parser error text>, and pid2-invalid-json: <parser message> on HTTP. Also pid2-schedule-needs-unmet: <routine>/<line>, pid2-schedule-wait-socket: <error>, protocol-kernel-field-missing:<field>, protocol-kernel-definition-missing:<index>, and pid2-command-wake-persist-failed: <error>.

first_missing_signal.meaning: HTTP refusal field, identical to firstMissingSignal on that refusal. Open forms are the same HTTP refusal forms described for firstMissingSignal.
